Chapter 3.2 (pp. 70-90) gives Kayaw syllable structure (only CVT and CCVT, open syllables), 22 consonants, 10 vowels and four contrastive tones (high, high-mid, mid, low; p. 85); pp. 87-88 discuss tone-sequence restrictions on two- and three-syllable words. The words 'stress', 'prominence', 'sesquisyllable', 'minor syllable' do not occur anywhere in the thesis (the two hits for 'accent' are the dialect sense, p. 12). downloaded from the the Internet Archive copy of the former Payap thesis archive (https://web.archive.org/web/20180329145459id_/https://inter.payap.ac.th/wp-content/uplo…

sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Kayaw column is from J. Fraser Bennett's unpublished field notes (p. i). Comparative method assumes Karenic is 'basically a monosyllabic language' and compares only the root syllable (p. 15; fn. 18 notes Matisoff's sesquisyllabic root). Live SIL URL is behind an automated-access block; downloaded via the Internet Archive (20220507070305).
